reading.body:
James Green's 31 AI lobbying filings are concentrated in telecommunications: CTIA, Lumen, Verizon, and AT&T together account for 26 of the 31 client mentions.

The pattern is a single lobbyist carrying AI filings for the carriers and their trade association. CTIA alone appears on 10 filings, Lumen on 8, Verizon and AT&T on 4 each. IAC and Match Group, the two non-carrier clients, account for 5 between them. The bill list runs to 12 separate measures, all named in filings dated 2025 or later, which places the activity in the current Congress rather than in a settled record.

For AI specifically, this matters because telecom carriers are the physical layer beneath compute. They own the fiber, the data centers, and the interconnection that training and inference traffic moves across. When the same lobbyist files on AI bills for CTIA, Verizon, AT&T, and Lumen, the interests being represented are those of the network operators whose infrastructure AI depends on, not of model developers or application vendors.

What the data does not show is what any of these filings argue. It records that a bill was named, not whether the client supported or opposed it, and it does not say what provisions the bills contain. It also covers one lobbyist at one firm, so it cannot describe the wider lobbying effort, only this person's share of it.
